sections.description:
OptiPub synchronizes content from the OptiPub platform to your WordPress installation. Creates custom post types for Articles, Resources, Reports, Videos, and Editors with automated sync every 5 minutes via WP-Cron.

Features: Secure API authentication, widget integration, tag management, redirect handling, and theme template integration.

Source Code for Minified Files

This plugin includes one minified JavaScript file (public/js/video.js) which is a third-party library. The source code for this minified file is publicly available:

Video.js v4.6.3 (Location: public/js/video.js)
* Source Code Repository: https://github.com/videojs/video.js/tree/v4.6.3
* License: Apache 2.0
* Documentation: https://docs.videojs.com/

All other JavaScript and CSS files in this plugin (public/js/archive-filters.js, public/js/gtm.js, public/js/init.js, public/js/login-forms.js, public/js/navigation-collapse.js, and public/css/subscribers.css) are provided in their original, unminified source code format and are fully human-readable.

External services

This plugin connects to several external services to provide functionality. The following services are used:

Google Tag Manager

This plugin connects to Google Tag Manager to provide tag management and analytics functionality. Google Tag Manager is needed to track website analytics and manage marketing tags when a publication has Google Tag Manager containers configured in the OptiPub platform.

It sends the Google Tag Manager container ID to www.googletagmanager.com on every page load where the plugin is active and GTM containers are configured. Once loaded, Google Tag Manager may collect visitor data according to the tags configured in your GTM container (this behavior is controlled by your GTM configuration, not by this plugin).

This service is provided by Google LLC: https://www.google.com/analytics/tag-manager/use-policy/, https://policies.google.com/privacy.

YouTube

This plugin may embed YouTube videos when video content is configured to use YouTube as the video player. YouTube embeds are needed to display video content on your website.

It sends the video ID to youtube.com/embed only when displaying video content configured to use YouTube. YouTube may collect visitor data according to their privacy policy when videos are embedded and played (this behavior is controlled by YouTube, not by this plugin).

This service is provided by Google LLC (YouTube): https://www.youtube.com/static?template=terms, https://policies.google.com/privacy.

Wistia

This plugin may embed Wistia videos when video content is configured to use Wistia as the video player. Wistia embeds are needed to display video content on your website.

It sends the video ID to fast.wistia.net only when displaying video content configured to use Wistia. Wistia may collect visitor data according to their privacy policy when videos are embedded and played (this behavior is controlled by Wistia, not by this plugin).

This service is provided by Wistia, Inc.: https://wistia.com/terms, https://wistia.com/privacy.

OptiPub API

This plugin connects to the OptiPub API service to synchronize content, publications, resources, videos, editors, tags, and redirects from the OptiPub platform to your WordPress installation. The API connection is needed to keep your WordPress site in sync with content managed in OptiPub.

It sends authenticated API requests to your configured OptiPub domain (typically https://.app.optipub.com) during content synchronization. API requests include your encrypted API token for authentication. Content synchronization occurs automatically via WP-Cron at configured intervals (default: every 5 minutes). The plugin also creates edit links to OptiPub content management pages when viewing content in the WordPress admin.

This service is provided by OptiPub. Please refer to your OptiPub service agreement for terms of use and privacy policy.

Third Party Libraries

This plugin includes one minified JavaScript library for video functionality:

  • Video.js v4.6.3 – Used for video player functionality
    • Source Code Repository: https://github.com/videojs/video.js/tree/v4.6.3
    • License: Apache 2.0
    • Location in Plugin: public/js/video.js
    • Documentation: https://docs.videojs.com/

The source code for this minified library is publicly available at the GitHub repository link above. This plugin does not include any custom build process – the minified file is used directly from the Video.js project.

OptiPub Introduction

OptiPub is used to sync OptiPub Resources to a WordPress Installation. The plugin schedules the WP-Cron event ‘optipub_sync’ to sync OptiPub Publications, Resources, Videos, Pages, Custom Content, Editors, Tags, and Redirects.

The plugin creates Custom Post Types (CPT’s) of following types: Articles, Resources, Reports, Videos, and Editors. Resources synced to these post types will store OptiPub metadata and properties in the wp_postmeta table of WordPress’s existing database. OptiPub Tags attached to these resources are saved as WordPress Categories.

WordPress Widgets can be created with OptiPub Custom Content from the OptiPub Admin page in the WordPress Admin Console.

Prepare

From the WordPress Admin panel go to Settings > General and use the Timezone drop down to select ‘New York’ or your desired Timezone. Then click [Save Changes].

You are able to use any timezone in WordPress, because OptiPub syncs with UTC. But OptiPub displays dates in EST. So if you don’t select ‘New York’ you may notice the website dates are different from OptiPub dates.

WordPress will automatically convert your post_date and post_modified to the selected Timezone. But you must do this before syncing data.

Installation

Before installing the plugin, we need to bundle the plugin for installation, which involves following two steps:

  1. Run composer install
  2. Zip the plugin.

Then from the WordPress Admin panel:

  1. Navigate to the Plugins page of the WordPress
  2. On the top of the page select Add New
  3. After you navigate to the new plugin page you need to select the Upload Plugin button.
  4. The page will require uploading the plugin as a zipped file.
  5. Click Install Plugin and the plugin should install. (Note: In default WP installations the max file upload is small and that needs to update as described below)
  6. Activate the plugin (Note: If installing in bitnami, before activating the plugin ensure the ownership and permissions are set as explained below)
  7. Activate the plugins associated custom theme before configuring the plugin (Note: if you miss this step, the widgets won’t be registered by the plugin and you will need to register them manually by navigating to WordPress Widget admin page)
  8. Configure the plugin from the OptiPub Admin page.

Bitnami permissions and configurations

To increase the upload file size run do the following:

  1. sudo -i
  2. sudo nano /opt/bitnami/php/etc/php.ini
  3. find and update upload_max_filesize variable, eg. upload_max_filesize = 128M
  4. Restart bitnami: sudo /opt/bitnami/ctlscript.sh restart

After the plugin has been installed, we need to set the permissions of the bitnami server environment. A set of commands
are needed to change the permissions of the plugin folders in WordPress. This will allow the proper activation and
configuration of the settings required from the plugin. For example, on uninstallation, the vendor files from the
composer need to be deleted since they are part of the plugin. This is currently not supported since the vendor files
are hidden files and PHP alone cannot delete them due to the Linux distro default settings.

In order to make the needed configurations, the following set of commands needs to be executed before activation.

Note: these commands are applying the permissions and ownership changes to all of the WP plugins. Update them if you need them to update only the OptiPub plugin.

  1. sudo find /home/bitnami/apps/wordpress/htdocs/wp-content/plugins/ -type d -exec chmod 775 {} \;
  2. sudo find /home/bitnami/apps/wordpress/htdocs/wp-content/plugins/ -type f -exec chmod 664 {} \;
  3. sudo chown -R bitnami:daemon /home/bitnami/apps/wordpress/htdocs/wp-content/plugins/

With those commands, you will set the user and group to binami:daemon, and you will change the permissions of the files to 664 and the permissions of the folders to 775.

  • 664 sets read and write permissions for user and Group, and provides read to Others.
  • 775 essential command that assigns read, write, and execute permission to a specific user, group, or others.

Activation

After the Plugin is installed in the WordPress environment, we need to activate the plugin in order to use. On the WordPress admin dashboard, navigate the left side menu of WordPress and click on the Plugins link. This will redirect to the installed WP plugins and on the list, there should be a plugin called – OptiPub. If this is not the case then something has gone wrong during the installation of the plugin.

After activating the WP Plugin a new green colored menu item should appear on the left bottom side with the name OptiPub Admin from where you can configure and run the plugin.

Activation Processes

During the plugin activation a set of processes are executed in order for the plugin to have a correct enviornment and constants that are needed for further processing. These processes are:

  1. Override the WP_CRON_LOCK_TIMEOUT constant – Upon activation the first process is to locate the wp-config.php file and override the constant. More on this WP_CRON_LOCK_TIMEOUT. Note: This step may fail if installing the plugin in bitnami and permissions and ownership is not set. Before activating the plugin ensure the ownership and permissions are set as explained below.
  2. Generate the OPTIPUB_KEY encryption key – This process generates a random key that is used to encrypt the token. This key is stored in wp-config.php file with name OPTIPUB_KEY. During plugin (cron job) execution the key is used to encrypt and decrypt the token that is needed for making API calls.
  3. Change permalink structure – The last process of the activation is to change the permalink structure of the base posts. This is done in order to accommodate the permalink structure of the posts. The default permalink structure is %postname%, and this is further changed to /%category%/%postname%/. This was doen to accommodate the URL structure for static pages with multiple slugs in their path, eg. https://www.energyandcapital.com/pubs-detailed/bab where pubs-detailed/bab is the path defined in /pages OptiPub API.

OptiPub Admin Page

The newly created green icon on the menu represents the Admin Page that is used to migrate the data from the OptiPub API. The page contains two fields.

OptiPub Sync Options
1. OptiPub Domain – The HTTPS URL of the OptiPub API for loading and syncing content.
2. API Token – The provided API Token from OptiPub will be used to authenticate with the API. The value of the
token is encrypted and stored in the database. Whenever the value is needed it will be decrypted and used in the API
calls.
3. Home Page Template – In OptiPub create a home page template and page, then input the template name in this
field.
– OptiPub > Administration > Templates – create a template with ‘.php’ at the end of the name like ‘optipub_home_page.php’
– OptiPub > Content > Pages – create a page with the path ‘/’ and the template you created earlier.
– Optional – OptiPub > Content > Redirects – create a page with the path ‘home’ then create a redirect from ‘domain.com/home’ to ‘https://www.domain.com/’
4. Open Graph Image Link – Input a URL for a backup / default image to use when calling a resource that may not have an image. then you can create a function to return this image with:
function get_optipub_opengraph_image() {
return get_option(\OptiPub\Base\Constants::OPTIPUB_OPENGRAPH_IMAGE_LINK);
}
5. Publication Drop Down – The dropdown is generated only after the OptiPub Domain and API Token have been
provided and Save changes clicked. The plugin will then sync your OptiPub publications, and once you select
6. Publication Domain Id – This input field refers to the publication domain id. Each publication has a domain id
that is further used to retrieve redirects based on that publication. The field only accepts numbers(integers).

Copy Files To Theme (feature complete – documentation under construction)
View more documentation in the plugin ‘OptiPub Admin’ page in the WordPress Admin Console

  1. Files will be copied to [theme-directory]/inc/optipub
  2. Select which file categories you would like to copy to your theme. Then click [Copy Files].
  3. You can reference these files from their current location. Or use them as a guide to help integrate your theme with OptiPub features.

If copying the Helper Functions, then afterwards copy the content from [theme-directory]inc/optipub/php/add_to_bottom_of_functions.php.txt to your theme’s function.php file.

The include statements in this file are commented out, as well as any filter or action calls in the files referenced that may alter content or meta on your website.

Review the functions in the referenced files before uncommenting any filters or actions or the include statements in functions.php.

Custom Content Widget Sidebars (feature complete – documentation under construction)
View more documentation in the plugin ‘OptiPub Admin’ page in the WordPress Admin Console

OptiPub > Content > Custom Content – create a custom content macro in optipub.

Custom Content is synced to WordPress as wordpress options.

Click [Create a New Widget]

Title – used for WordPress Admin Console.
Sidebar ID – used to display your widget in your theme templates.
File Name – used to hold the WordPress Sidebar Widget content. Default content will be –
Description – used for WordPress Admin Console
Custom Content – the OptiPub custom content macro name.
Class Name – use this in CSS to modify your custom content.
Before Widget – HTML to add before widget.
After Widget – HTML to add after widget.
Before Title – HTML to add before title. If used your ‘Title’ will be displayed live with your widget.
After Title – HTML to add after title. If used your ‘Title’ will be displayed live with your widget.

How OptiPub Custom Content creates WordPress Sidebar Widgets

Widget Files will be created in your theme directory as:
[theme-directory]/inc/optipub/widget-templates/File Name

The default content for these files displays the wp_option that holds your custom content:
<?php echo get_option('{$custom_content_name}'); ?>

Include a widget in your theme template pages by adding this code:
if (is_active_sidebar('sidebar-id')) {
dynamic_sidebar('sidebar-id');
}

Save Changes Button

The Save changes button first validates the input fields for API Domain and token and then stores the data of the Optipub Domain,Api Token,Publication,Publication Domain,Header Pencil Ad Macro,Article bottom Ad Macro,Signup Sidebar Macro fields in wp_options table.

The Cron job get scheduled to run every 5 minutes during Save changes button click only if the Optipub Domain,Api Token, and Publication are provided correctly.

After the changes are saved an API call is made to the OptiPub, and the publication metadata is fetched such as the resources that compose the Custom Post Types of the WordPress application. The fetched metadata for resources is shown on the left menu of the WordPress admin console. New links are created based on the CPT’s created, and these links are shown with a green color to differentiate from other CPT’s created.

Clear Data Button

The clear data button provides functionality that clears the data imported from the resources. For example, all the
posts such as articles, resources, reports, etc, are deleted. The metadata of the publication still exists, but the
posts imported from the API are no longer in the database. The clear data button will stop and reschedule the cron job.
This is implemented as a measure to easily reset …
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/optipub/
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  3. Navigate to ‘OptiPub Admin’ in the WordPress admin menu
  4. Configure your OptiPub domain and API token
  5. Select publications to sync and click ‘Save Changes’
sections.faq:
What permissions do I need?

The plugin requires write permissions to your WordPress installation for creating custom post types and storing synced content.

How often does content sync?

By default, content syncs every 5 minutes. You can adjust this interval in the plugin constants.

Can I sync multiple publications?

Yes, you can select a primary publication and additional publications to sync simultaneously.

Is my API token secure?

Yes, API tokens are encrypted before storage and only decrypted when needed for API calls.

Can I customize the sync behavior?

Yes, the plugin provides extensive configuration options through constants and admin settings.

Save Changes Button

The Save changes button first validates the input fields for API Domain and token and then stores the data of the Optipub Domain,Api Token,Publication,Publication Domain,Header Pencil Ad Macro,Article bottom Ad Macro,Signup Sidebar Macro fields in wp_options table.

The Cron job get scheduled to run every 5 minutes during Save changes button click only if the Optipub Domain,Api Token, and Publication are provided correctly.

After the changes are saved an API call is made to the OptiPub, and the publication metadata is fetched such as the resources that compose the Custom Post Types of the WordPress application. The fetched metadata for resources is shown on the left menu of the WordPress admin console. New links are created based on the CPT’s created, and these links are shown with a green color to differentiate from other CPT’s created.

Clear Data Button

The clear data button provides functionality that clears the data imported from the resources. For example, all the
posts such as articles, resources, reports, etc, are deleted. The metadata of the publication still exists, but the
posts imported from the API are no longer in the database. The clear data button will stop and reschedule the cron job.
